previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and chronic tracheostomy was admitted for worsening odynophagia, green sputum, chest and throat pain, and dyspnea on exertion. She had recently completed a course of doxycycline for suspected MRSA tracheitis. On admission, she was afebrile with stable vitals and no radiographic abnormalities. Labs showed mild anemia but no leukocytosis. A deep tracheal sputum culture confirmed MRSA, and she was treated with a 7-day course of intravenous vancomycin. A CT neck showed no new inflammatory changes or fluid collection. A bedside swallow evaluation indicated mild oropharyngeal dysphagia without aspiration risk. Her symptoms improved, and she was transitioned to oral intake. Her tracheostomy tube was replaced after antibiotic completion as part of MRSA decolonization. She was discharged home with lidocaine for throat pain and instructions for home hygiene, with follow-up planned with infectious disease and pulmonary specialists.
